## Create and select columns

In this milestone, you'll write some of the code that was written for you in milestone 3.

1.  The events_formatted.parquet file is read in, named "events",  and filtered for health events. 
2.  Filter this further so you only have only one or 2 unique health events that are interesting to you.  The example in the solution is based on 'NAVEL' and 'SEPTIC' events, but choose anything you want. If it is not NAVEL and SEPTIC don't worry about the solutions not matching in this milestone.
3.  create a new variable named **floordate_month**. The logic to create this variable is: **floor_date(date_event, 'months')**
4.  arrange the data by 3 variables: the animal (id_animal), the event (event), and then the event date (date_event). 
5.  Pipe your events_formatted to the function fxn_add_event_counts(). This will add columns indicating the number of times the animal has had that event within the data set (event_count_animal) or within their lactation (event_count_lact). If you would like to see the code the creates these click on the function in your environment.
6.  create a new variable the is animal age in days at time of event. Name this variable "age_event"
7.  select all the variables below in the order you see them.

```{r}
#| label: recreation-import
#| 
events <- read_parquet(here::here("data/intermediate_files/events_formatted.parquet")) |>
  filter(event_type == "health")

events_filtered <- events |>
  filter(event %in% c("NAVEL", "SEPTIC")) |>
  mutate(
    floordate_month = floor_date(date_event, "months")
  ) |>
  arrange(id_animal, event, date_event) |>
  fxn_add_event_counts() |>
  mutate(
    age_event = as.numeric(date_event - date_birth),
    Disease = case_when(
      event == "NAVEL" ~ "Navel Ill",
      event == "SEPTIC" ~ "Septicemia",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    Treatment = case_when(
    remark %in% c("EXC+PEN", "EXCNL+PEN") ~ "Excenel + Penicillin",
    remark %in% c("BAY+PEN") ~ "Baytril + Penicillin",
    remark %in% c("PEN5.5", "PEN3.14", "PEN3.3", "PEN15.5", "PEN10.5") ~ "Penicillin",
    remark %in% c("PLY3.2", "PLY3.23", "PLY3.26") ~ "Polyflex",
    remark %in% c("X1.5P5.2") ~ "Unknown X + Penicillin",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    id_animal,
    event,
    date_event,
    floordate_month,
    event_count_animal,
    event_count_lact,
    age_event,
    remark,
    Disease,
    Treatment
  )

#did my new things work?
events_filtered|>
  count(Disease,Treatment)

# It did, but I apparently didn't catch all the treatment options becuase it's only showing penicillin - this helped me pull all remarks & incorporate them above
events_filtered|>
  count(Disease, remark, sort = TRUE)
```

### Step 2 - Disease and Treatments

Create 2 new variables for your events: Disease and Treatment.  Use case_when() and whichever columns you would like to create the best description.
Then use graphs, tables, or a combination to describe the timing your selected Disease(s), both over time and according to animal age or dim as appropriate. 
Show if there has been a change in the treatments used over time.

Below are a couple example graphics, but yours can be prettier.

```{r}
#| label: recreate-this
#| message: false

if (!require(magick, quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("magick")
  library(magick)
}

image_read("milestones_dairy/images/milestone4_disease_over_time.jpg")
image_read('milestones_dairy/images/milestone4_disease_by_phase.jpg')
knitr::include_graphics('milestones_dairy/images/milestone4_disease_over_time.jpg')
knitr::include_graphics('milestones_dairy/images/milestone4_disease_by_phase.jpg')

#Okay, now let's build some graphs

#Here's disease incidence over time parted out by Navel ill & Septicemia
events_filtered|>
  count(floordate_month,Disease)|>
  ggplot(aes(x=floordate_month, y=n, fill=Disease))+
  geom_col(position="dodge")+ #separates out bars rather than stacking them for each month
  labs(
    title="Navel ill & septicemia events over time",
    x="Month",
    y="Number of events",
    Fill="Disease"
  )

#And now by animal age
events_filtered|>
  ggplot(aes(x=Disease, y=age_event, fill=Disease)) +
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(
    title="Animal age at disease event",
    x="Disease",
    y="Age at event (days)",
    fill="Disease"
  )

#I don't like that boxplot, the spread is too wide. 
#Here is a histogram with 7-day bins up to 100 days of age - disease incidence dropped off dramatically after that point & stretched out the x-axis too much.
events_filtered |>
  filter(age_event<=100)|> #limits to age <100 days
  ggplot(aes(x = age_event, fill = Disease)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 7) + #binwidth = 7 days, so by week of age
  facet_wrap(vars(Disease), scales = "free_y") + #separates out each disease, free_y allows separate y axes for each disease process
  labs(
    title = "Age distribution of navel ill and septicemia events",
    x = "Age at event, days",
    y = "Number of events",
    fill = "Disease"
  )

#Now by treatment - we see a clear shift to penicillin from polyflex for treatment of both diseases - it would be nice to part out disease treatments
events_filtered |>
  mutate(year_event = year(date_event)) |>
  count(year_event, Treatment) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year_event, y = n, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Treatment use by year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of events",
    fill = "Treatment"
  )

#if we part them out by disease process
events_filtered |>
  mutate(year_event = year(date_event)) |> #takes out month & only counts toward year
  count(year_event, Disease,Treatment) |> #counts of treatment by disease per year
  ggplot(aes(x = year_event, y = n, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(vars(Disease))+
  labs(
    title = "Treatment use by year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of events",
    fill = "Treatment"
  )

#ChatGPT suggested using proportions instead, which I hate - scale is position="fill" part
events_filtered |>
  mutate(year_event = year(date_event)) |>
  count(year_event, Disease, Treatment) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year_event, y = n, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  facet_wrap(vars(Disease)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2020, 2026, by = 1) #forces labeled years for all years in dataset
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Proportion of treatments used by year by disease",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Proportion of events",
    fill = "Treatment"
  )

?geom_bar()
```
